transcript.content: Hello. What brings you into the clinic today?

I feel like I just can’t keep my projects organized anymore, no matter how many lists and calendars I use. It's gotten to the point where it's really affecting my job, and I just feel completely overwhelmed.
Have you struggled with these organization and attention difficulties since childhood, or is this a relatively new change for you?

It actually goes back to my childhood, though things became much worse after my promotion about two years ago. Even in elementary school, my report cards said I daydreamed and couldn't stay in my seat, and my mom always got frustrated because I'd wander off halfway through chores or homework unless she constantly reminded me.
Along with feeling overwhelmed, do you find yourself constantly worrying about many different areas of your life, even when there is no immediate problem?

I don't really find myself constantly worrying about other areas of my life when there isn't an immediate problem. My stress and overwhelm are very specifically tied to my work, keeping up with my projects, and the constant fear of letting people down.
Aside from feeling overwhelmed by work, have you been experiencing a persistently low or sad mood, or a loss of interest in things you normally enjoy?

No, I haven't really experienced a persistently sad mood or lost interest in my usual hobbies. I do feel highly stressed, anxious, and overwhelmed, but it is specifically regarding my work performance and trying to keep up.
Do you currently experience physical restlessness, like difficulty sitting still or constant fidgeting, or do you tend to make impulsive decisions or interrupt others during conversations?

Yes, absolutely. I get so squirmy in long meetings that I have to make excuses to get up and get water because sitting still makes me feel like I’m crawling out of my skin. I also constantly jump in with answers on calls before people finish speaking, and I sometimes find myself barging into coworkers' conversations without realizing it until afterward.

Other primary conditions, such as generalized anxiety disorder or depressive episodes, have been ruled out as the primary cause of these symptoms.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with a long-standing history of both inattentive and hyperactive-impulsive symptoms dating back to childhood (elementary school) that have persisted into adulthood. These symptoms cause significant functional impairment, particularly in her occupational functioning following a recent promotion. Alternative explanations such as Generalized Anxiety Disorder or Major Depressive Disorder were ruled out as her anxiety and distress are secondary to her ADHD symptoms and work performance.
